name: Zacharias' Domain
placement: The named Forest of Shadows province in Ostland.
description: A secluded Necrarch enclave conducts necromantic research and raids surrounding settlements for subjects and corpses. Suggested reform: **Necromancer's Domain**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Zacharias](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Zacharias). For strict 2502 chronology, begin under Melkhior and allow Zacharias to succeed him later; starting with Zacharias is a deliberate timeline adjustment.
flag_brief: Ivory fanged skull, crimson bat wings and an open grimoire on midnight violet, antique gold trim
enclave_description: Zacharias the Everliving commands the dead from a hidden tower in the Forest of Shadows. Once the pupil of the Necrarch Melkhior, he coveted his master's forbidden books and wrested the tower from him through necromantic war. Now corpse-bearing servants pass beneath the trees, and the settlements around his refuge supply unwilling subjects for experiments intended to outlast the living world.

name: Dieter Helsnicht's Domain
placement: Ferlangen, a separate forest stronghold east of the Forest of Shadows province.
description: A human necromancer's fortified domain threatens northern Ostland with undead armies and terror raids. Suggested reform: **Necromancer's Domain**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Dieter Helsnicht](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Dieter_Helsnicht); Ferlangen is the proposed map foothold for his concealed forest domain.
flag_brief: A bone-white manticore rampant above a red flaming skull on black, dull silver border
enclave_description: Dieter Helsnicht, the Doom Lord of Middenheim, broods in a concealed stronghold in the forests around Ferlangen. In 2499, Valmir von Raukov defeated him at the Battle of Wolfen River, but the necromancer survived to gather the dead once more. His servants strip graves and waylay travelers, rebuilding the host with which he means to avenge another humiliation at Imperial hands.

name: Cluster Eye Tribe
placement: Deinste, in the forest north of Black Pit. Replaces impassable Black Pit (25); the earlier Rosche alternative is also avoided because Drakwald's capital ownership is inconsistent.
description: Spider-worshipping Forest Goblins guard the approaches to their sacred pit, ambushing neighboring armies and raiding villages. Suggested reform: **Greenskin Tribe**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Black Pit and its tribes](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Black_Pit); the playable foothold is outside the impassable pit itself.
flag_brief: An ochre eight-legged spider with a cluster of red eyes, dark blue field and black angular border
enclave_description: Vish Venombarb leads the Cluster Eye Tribe through the spider-haunted woods of Deinste, near the approaches to the Black Pit. An experienced slaver, he trades captured humans and Ungors to the Night Goblins who dwell below. His Forest Goblins ride enormous spiders through branches no patrol can easily reach, carrying villagers away to the tribe's pens and sacred feeding grounds.

name: Brass Keep
placement: Dripping Peak, the unowned province targeted by the mod's Brass Keep colonization decision; retain the current map name in this list.
description: A Nurgle-infested fortress garrison menaces the Middle Mountains approaches. Retain the existing Bjornling and Nurglite population. Suggested reforms: **Mandate of Chaos + Chaos Warband**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Brass Keep](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Brass_Keep), following the mod's existing Nurglite premise; a garrison enclave, not another Festus country.
flag_brief: A corroded brass three-towered keep topped by three round plague rings on dark olive green
enclave_description: Brass Keep rises above the approaches to Dripping Peak, sheltering a Nurglite garrison among the Middle Mountains. Egil Rusthand's Bjornling warriors endure behind its foul walls, emerging to seize provisions and drag captives uphill. Below them, abandoned farms and diseased livestock mark the reach of a fortress whose strength grows wherever fear keeps our patrols away.

name: House von Wittgenstein
placement: Wittgendorf, representing the village and nearby Castle Wittgenstein in Reikland.
description: A corrupted noble household hides mutation, warpstone contamination, and forbidden experiments behind its legal baronial status. Suggested reform: **Chaos Undivided Monarchy**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Castle Wittgenstein](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Castle_Wittgenstein); Chaos Undivided represents the corrupted household, while ordinary villagers can retain their Imperial faith.
flag_brief: A black raven with one twisted claw carrying a green falling star on quartered ivory and dark red
enclave_description: Above Wittgendorf, the von Wittgensteins shelter behind the rights of an ancient barony. Dagmar brought a warpstone meteorite to the castle in 2402; the family withdrew from society as corruption spread through its estate. Margritte now pursues necromantic experiments behind the gates, while the villagers below bear the hunger, mutation, and disappearances that noble privilege conceals.

name: Cult of the Red Crown
placement: Delberz, a wooded Middenland foothold toward the Drakwald; substitutes for the earlier Fassberg (100) proposal because Drakwald's starting capital ownership is inconsistent.
description: A concealed cult organizes mutants and Beastmen against Imperial authority, turning a secret network into an armed forest enclave. Suggested reform: **Tzeentchian Theocracy**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Cult of the Red Crown](https://warhammerfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Cult_of_the_Red_Crown); territorial rule and the exact camp are proposed.
flag_brief: A blood-red crown with nine flame-like points surrounding one gold eye on blue-black, thin red edge
history_file: history/countries/E05 - Cult of the Red Crown.txt
enclave_description: The Red Crown maintains a hidden foothold in the woods around Delberz. Its Master of Change directs scattered sorcerers and apprentices who shelter mutants and bargain with Beastmen in the name of Tzeentch. Those rescued from the witch hunters become recruits for a greater rising, while messengers carry forbidden teachings between forest camps and unsuspecting towns.

name: Slugtongue's Warherd
placement: Nattern Forest in Stirland, beside productive Imperial farmland.
description: A famine-bringing Beastman warherd blights harvests and lures desperate defenders into forest ambushes. Suggested reform: **Beastman Horde**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Slugtongue](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Slugtongue); the fixed starting province is a design choice.
flag_brief: An ivory horned goat skull vomiting three black locust silhouettes over yellow dead wheat on black-green
enclave_description: Slugtongue's warherd lurks beneath the diseased boughs of Nattern Forest. Vermin crawl through the Bray-Shaman's ruined body, and his passing brings failed harvests, dying herds, and the hunger that empties villages. His Beastmen watch the roads for starving refugees and supply wagons, striking when famine has weakened those who would otherwise drive them from the woods.

name: Drycha's Wargrove
placement: Borkum, in the Gryphon Woods; already has Dryads culture and the Asrai religion in the mod.
description: Hostile forest spirits reject surrounding human rule and strike at settlements encroaching on their woods. Suggested reform: **The Asrai Pantheon Tribe**.
basis: Total War adaptation — [Wargrove of Woe](https://totalwarwarhammer.fandom.com/wiki/Wargrove_of_Woe); Gryphon Wood follows the game's placement.
flag_brief: An ivory screaming tree face with branching antlers and crimson leaves on deep cold turquoise
enclave_description: Drycha gathers embittered forest spirits in the Gryphon Wood around Borkum. The Branchwraith despises the Elves' claim to rule the forests and sees human clearings as another wound cut into living wood. Her dryads stalk the margins of farms and logging camps, leaving torn bodies among the roots as a warning against the next axe or plough.

name: Morghur's Warherd
placement: Beaussons, in Bretonnia's Forest of Arden; retains the original proposed foothold.
description: The Shadowgave's corrupting warherd turns Arden into a source of mutation and raids against Bretonnian settlements. Suggested reform: **Beastman Horde**.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Morghur](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Morghur); restored from the earlier Empire-and-neighbors shortlist, with its Bretonnian geography retained.
flag_brief: An ivory malformed horned skull with curling root-like horns and a red vertical wound on dark brown-black
enclave_description: Morghur the Shadowgave haunts the Forest of Arden around Beaussons, drawing Beastmen to the corruption that seeps from his presence. Trees twist, flesh changes, and the boundaries between beast and man lose their meaning wherever he lingers. His warherd descends on Bretonnian settlements for slaughter and sacrifice, then withdraws into woodland that grows more hostile with every passing season.

name: Red Duke's Exiles
placement: Châlons approaches on the Aquitaine side, at Derrevin Libre; foothold south of the forest rather than the named Chalons province.
description: An exiled vampire war court threatening Aquitaine; geographically distinct from Mallobaude's existing Mousilion.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Red Duke](https://warhammerfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Duke).
flag_brief: A silver dragon winding around a downward-pointing sword on blood-red with black corners
enclave_description: The Red Duke keeps an exiled court in Derrevin Libre, nursing his claim to Aquitaine. He returned from the crusades as a vampire and was defeated and entombed after Ceren Field in 1454, but the grave failed to hold him. His undead retainers now raid the countryside, turning an ancient knightly grievance into a war that the living must fight again.

name: Aucassin's Household
placement: A rural castle at Yremy, inland from Mousilion.
description: A wealthy vampire noble's household, feeding on the countryside and competing for influence over the surrounding duchy.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Aucassin](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Aucassin); independence is proposed.
flag_brief: Canonical heraldry adaptation: exactly three BLACK five-petaled flowers arranged two above one on an ivory white field, small black fleur-de-lis below; no skulls
enclave_description: Aucassin's household extends its influence into Yremy from the courtly world of Mousillon. At Chateau Hane, the vampire presides over poetry, fine furnishings, and the traffic across the Grismerie; his gracious manners persuade many guests to overlook what sustains him. Wealth buys discretion and fresh victims, while armed retainers ensure that the surrounding villages continue to serve their elegant predator.

name: Brachnar's Laboratory
placement: Montlac's wooded approaches north of Quenelles; proposed laboratory site outside the ducal capital.
description: A Necrarch research enclave whose corpse collectors clash with Bretonnian villages and Kemmler's servants.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Quenelles history](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Queneles), which records Brachnar's conflict with Kemmler.
flag_brief: An ivory skull inside a ring of nine copper candles above a green alchemical retort on wine-black
enclave_description: Brachnar the Damned hides his experiments in Montlac, still consumed by hatred of Heinrich Kemmler. The Lichemaster reduced him to dust in 2424, but an unwitting hedge wizard restored him in 2464; in 2480, Brachnar ambushed his old enemy in the Vaults. His servants now gather corpses and occult supplies for the next reckoning, leaving the neighboring settlements to pay for his patience.

name: Bowmen of Bergerac
placement: Vignoble's Aquitanian woodland; substitute for Bergerac, which has no separately named province.
description: Bertrand's outlaw band becomes a peasant refuge. Raids target oppressive nobles, not indiscriminately all Bretonnians.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Bertrand](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Bertrand).
flag_brief: A white longbow crossed by three gold arrows on forest green, small golden grail above
enclave_description: Bertrand the Brigand shelters the Bowmen of Bergerac among the woods and vineyards of Vignoble. A ploughman who took up the bow when his lord's heir would not defend the peasants, he slew the monster of Chateau Mal and refused to settle into a knight's life. His followers protect common folk and strike at abusive nobles, making them heroes to villagers and outlaws to the authorities they defy.

name: Coeddil's Wildwood
placement: Cythral Forest, in Athel Loren's enclosed southern Wildwood.
description: Hostile forest spirits oppose Elven rule. Begin as a contained enclave; breaking the waystones should release their expansion.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Coeddil](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Coeddil); his imprisonment is essential.
flag_brief: A bone-colored ancient gnarled tree with a single red eye, broken stone ring at its roots on near-black green
enclave_description: Coeddil remains imprisoned within the Cythral Forest, behind the waystones that contain the Wildwood. After he attacked the King's Glade to prevent Orion's rebirth, Ariel defeated the ancient Treeman and bound him with his followers. The spirits within still nurse their hatred of Elven rule, and every disturbance of the boundary risks giving that ancient fury a path into the world.

name: Knights of Irrana
placement: Llaqueno, in the Irrana Mountains; a highland fortress outside the existing capital.
description: An Estalian Blood Knight order sustains itself through tribute, abducted recruits, and violent challenges to neighboring rulers.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Knights of Irrana](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Knights_of_Irrana); not the existing human country Irrana.
flag_brief: An ivory armored gauntlet clasping a red chalice, crossed silver lances behind on black and burgundy
enclave_description: The Knights of Irrana maintain a blood-hungry brotherhood in Llaqueno under Armand de Sangrivage. Their order abandoned Myrmidia when its Grand Master judged Abhorash's martial teachings greater and led his knights into undeath. They still observe the forms of knightly honor, but their challenges, demands for tribute, and search for worthy recruits leave the surrounding countryside at the mercy of immortal warriors.

name: Long Drong's Anchorage
placement: Caprio, a coastal foothold in the Sartosa island group.
description: Slayer pirates operate an armed independent harbor, extorting merchant shipping and fighting whoever refuses their terms.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Long Drong's Slayer Pirates](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Long_Drong%27s_Slayer_Pirates).
flag_brief: Lore heraldry adaptation: a foaming silver ALE FLAGON above two crossed flintlock pistols on black, small orange beard-knot below; no skull
enclave_description: Long Drong's Slayer Pirates keep their powder, plunder, and repaired hulls at Caprio. The captain and his crew took the Slayer oath after the loss of the Barrel of Ale and its precious Dwarf brew, then seized the pirate ship they rebuilt as the Fair Fregar. Their anchorage supports voyages in pursuit of treasure, pay chests, and a death worthy of their shame.

name: Shadewraith Haven
placement: Grotta, a sheltered Tilean coastal foothold beside Tobaro.
description: Vangheist's ghost crew receives a terrestrial refuge, turning a trading coast into a predatory supernatural enclave.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Vangheist](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Vangheist); the haven and Nagashi mapping are proposals.
flag_brief: A pale sea-green spectral galleon above a silver skull and crossed anchors on deep navy
enclave_description: Vangheist's spectral crew haunts the coast of Grotta, where the Shadewraith finds shelter beyond the reach of ordinary harbor law. The ghost ship and its dead sailors bring terror to sea lanes that living captains must still navigate. Wreckage and abandoned landing places mark their shoreward reach, while the promise of lost cargo draws fresh victims toward the haven.

name: Golgfag's Winter Camp
placement: Heldegrad, on the northern Border Princes approaches below the Black Mountains.
description: A mercenary company entrenches itself in a fortified camp, demanding provisions and selling violence to rival princes.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Golgfag's mercenary identity](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/List_of_Ogres); a fixed base is invented.
flag_brief: An ivory ogre jaw with a gold coin between its teeth over crossed cleavers on oxblood
enclave_description: Golgfag Maneater has established a winter camp near Heldegrad, bringing veteran Ogres and enormous appetites into the Border Princes. The famous mercenary sells his strength wherever the bargain suits him, and rival rulers court his company while fearing its upkeep. His followers demand meat, shelter, and payment from nearby settlements; a village that cannot supply the camp may become its next meal.

name: Wintertooth
placement: The map's Lair of the Troll King, in Trollheim on the Norsca–Troll Country frontier; replaces the earlier broad northeastern Troll Country placement.
description: Throgg unites monsters against human dominance. A small starting lair can grow into a kingdom of displaced creatures.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Throgg](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Throgg) and [Troll Country](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Troll_Country).
flag_brief: A large bone-white tusked troll skull wearing a jagged iron crown on icy slate blue
enclave_description: Throgg rules from the Lair of the Troll King, gathering creatures that human warlords normally hunt, enslave, or drive before their armies. His unnatural intelligence allows him to turn a Troll's hunger and strength toward ambitions his brutish kin could never imagine. Trolls and other monsters answer his summons, raiding the neighboring lands as he prepares a world in which mankind is the prey.

name: Beasts of Telldros
placement: Skraevold, on the wooded Troll Country–Norsca frontier.
description: The surviving monsters of a defeated Chaos army become an unusually leaderless, destructive enclave of spawn and beasts.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Beasts of Telldros](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Beasts_of_Telldros); permanent camp proposed.
flag_brief: A crimson three-headed many-horned beast silhouette over a broken bronze shield on pale ash gray
enclave_description: The Beasts of Telldros range from Skraevold under the Dragon Ogre Kharzulg Stormscar. Their warband descends from the monsters that survived Telldros' defeat at Icicle Pass, when Dragon Ogres rallied the scattered spawn and other creatures into a vengeful pack. Markus Wulfhart hunted the beasts across Norsca in 2501 without bringing them to heel; their raids still leave shattered camps and stripped carcasses behind.

name: Sog'Kog's Feeding Ground
placement: Fort Straghov in northern Troll Country; the feeding ground surrounds a captured border fort.
description: A two-headed mutant monster dominates lesser scavengers; winter feeding raids distinguish it from an ordinary human warband.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Sog'Kog](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Sog%27Kog); followers and territory are invented.
flag_brief: A two-headed green troll silhouette with ivory tusks above two crossed bones on dark ochre
enclave_description: The two-headed mutant Troll Sog'Kog feeds in the country around Fort Straghov. Scavengers and lesser brutes gather in the wake of his kills, turning a single monster's hunting ground into a refuge for creatures driven from settled lands. Livestock, baggage animals, and isolated travelers disappear along the approaches, while the fort's name offers little comfort to those beyond its walls.

name: Black Ogham Circle
placement: Dunnok, an inland Albion foothold within the Truthsayers' territory.
description: Dark Emissaries establish a competing ritual authority, sacrificing rival clans' captives to undermine the Truthsayers' protection.
basis: **Made up;** inspired by [Albion's Dark Emissaries](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Albion).
flag_brief: Three black standing stones with an ivory eye cut into the center stone, pale purple storm disc on moss-gray
enclave_description: Maelor Blackreed's Dark Emissaries hold a hidden circle of standing stones near Dunnok. They corrupt Albion's sacred sites with captive sacrifices, seeking to turn the old powers of the island against its Truthsayers. Bog paths carry prisoners into the mist, and the settlements around the circle learn that the stones which once guarded their land now shelter its enemies.

name: Brothers' Giant Moot
placement: Everpeak, in Albion's interior; proposed giant gathering ground.
description: Bologs and Cachtorr provide the seed for a giant coalition demanding cattle tribute from nearby human tribes.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Bologs and Cachtorr](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Bologs); the moot and faith mapping are invented.
flag_brief: Two immense ivory clubs crossed beneath a gold sun disc on peat green, Celtic angular trim
enclave_description: Bologs and his brother Cachtorr have become the center of a Giant gathering in Everpeak. Other wandering Giants meet them among the heights, where old stones and open pasture offer space for feasting far from human walls. Nearby communities surrender cattle to keep the brothers content, but each new guest at the moot brings another appetite that tribute must satisfy.

name: Rime-Eater Clans
placement: Mount Hellspire, a glacier refuge in the Norscan mountains.
description: Snow-dwelling beastfolk seize winter migration routes, raiding Norse livestock and attacking mountain mines.
basis: **Made up;** uses the mod's existing Ymir culture.
flag_brief: A white horned shaggy beast head above a jagged ice mountain on dark glacial blue
enclave_description: Hrogg Rimehide leads the Rime-Eater Clans through the snows of Mount Hellspire. These Ymir beastfolk shelter in frozen passes above the Norse settlements, descending when storms hide their movement. Stolen livestock sustains their camps, while attacks on mines and mountain caravans prevent the lowland chiefs from claiming the routes they regard as their own.

name: Rabidscar Remnant
placement: Snag, an Underway foothold on the Bretonnian side of the Grey Mountains; substitute for the Black Chasm, which has no separately named province.
description: Survivors reclaim an old clan seat, attacking whoever now controls its tunnels. Survival as an organized state is speculative.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Clan Rabidscar's former seat](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/List_of_Skaven_clans); remnant invented.
flag_brief: A jagged black rat triangle slashed by three red claw scars on dirty parchment, rusty red edge
enclave_description: Furblak's Rabidscar remnant gnaws at the tunnels around Snag. The clan once held power in the Black Chasm, but internal strife drove its ruler and his followers into exile. They have returned to the underways with old grudges and too few resources, stealing supplies and murdering rivals as Furblak searches for a route back to the seat he lost.

name: Drachenfels Restorationists
placement: Castle Drachenfels itself, including its outlying vaults and approaches.
description: A necromantic cult occupies the cursed castle's approaches and tries to recreate its master's terror.
basis: **Made up;** does not identify the mod's amnesiac Nameless country with Constant Drachenfels.
flag_brief: A white skull embedded in a black craggy castle, crimson moon behind on deep violet
enclave_description: Albrecht Gravenhorst gathers necromancers and tomb robbers within Castle Drachenfels. His followers seek to restore the dread associated with its former master, scavenging the ruins for instruments of torment and scraps of forbidden learning. Captives vanish behind the broken walls, and the neighboring countryside finds that a ruined fortress can still command obedience when its cellars hold the dead.

name: Ember-Script Heretics
placement: Vogg, a tunnel and forge enclave in the Vaults.
description: Outcast rune-workers bind spirits into stolen engines, raid ancestral workshops, and trade weapons to the holds' enemies.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A copper anvil bearing a glowing ember-red forbidden rune and chained flame on charcoal
enclave_description: Durgan Emberbrand's renegade Dwarfs work hidden forges beneath Vogg. Having turned from the Ancestor Gods to Hashut, they carve forbidden runes and bind spirits into engines that orthodox Runesmiths would condemn. Stolen tools, ore, and captives keep the workshops burning, while raiding parties descend on neighboring mines to obtain what honest trade will no longer provide.

name: Badwater Hagdom
placement: Felwing Cave and the river channels on the northern edge of the Mourkain marsh basin; a proposed Blight Water foothold.
description: A hag-led troll community controls river passage and attacks Greenskin rafts, caravans, and nearby settlements.
basis: **Made up name and polity;** [the river's hag-led troll tribes](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Blight_Water) are canonical.
flag_brief: A pale green hag-like troll face with ivory tusks above three silver river waves on black-green
enclave_description: Grulma Bogbelly rules a River Troll gathering in the flooded hollows of Felwing Cave. The hag's followers watch the Blight Water crossings from reed beds and foul pools, overturning rafts and dragging pack animals beneath the surface. Caravans that survive the river must still pass the trails to her lair, where discarded cargo and gnawed bones mark the cost of her appetite.

name: Boglar-Fimir Compact
placement: Stinkwater Fen in the marsh basin southwest of Mourkain; uses the Badlands site, not the similarly named Marsh of Madness in Lustria.
description: Swamp Goblins and Fimir combine traps, fog, and night raids against neighboring Orcs and undead.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Boglars' rumored Fimir alliance](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Boglar); the compact's formal organization is invented.
flag_brief: A single gold eye above a pair of crossed short knives and reeds on dark swamp green
enclave_description: In Stinkwater Fen, Skibbit Mireclaw's Boglars share their refuge with Fimir who cloak the marsh in concealing mist. The Goblins prepare traps and hidden paths while their larger allies strike from waters too deep for ordinary patrols. Their uneasy compact survives on plunder, drawing captives and supplies from Orc camps, passing armies, and the margins of nearby settlements.

name: Black Lantern Prospectors
placement: Redstone Underpass, beneath Karak Azul's southern approaches; proposed abandoned mine workings.
description: Undead miners reopen exhausted seams for a necromantic overseer, stealing bodies and ore from living holds.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A black lantern with a spectral emerald flame between two ivory miner picks on slate gray
enclave_description: Borri Graveshaft's dead miners still work the abandoned seams of Redstone Underpass. Lanterns move through galleries that living Dwarfs have long since forsaken, and the sound of picks continues without rest or shift change. The prospectors seize ore, tools, and bodies from neighboring workings, pressing each new acquisition into a mining enterprise whose laborers are never allowed to leave.

name: Golden Magus' Refuge
placement: Al-Qayid, a coastal refuge just south of Copher; a mainland substitute because no separate usable island is mapped immediately offshore.
description: A wizard's corsair court defies the One Faith's prohibition on spirit bargains and competes with coastal rulers.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Golden Magus](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Golden_Magus); island and religious identity proposed.
flag_brief: A golden oil lamp emitting a turquoise curling djinn plume above two gold stars on deep indigo
enclave_description: The Golden Magus keeps a corsair refuge in Al-Qayid, where stolen cargo pays for sorcery and the service of bound djinn. His reputation as a master of spirits draws sailors who would rather bargain with an uncanny patron than submit to the Prophet's laws. From these sheltered landings, his followers prey on coastal trade and defy the One Faith's condemnation of their pacts.

name: Alhazred's Observatory
placement: Sharikah, on the eastern Arabian desert frontier toward Nehekhara.
description: A forbidden scholarly enclave studies necromancy and binds djinn, supplying a direct ideological enemy to the Prophet's followers.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Abdul Alhazred](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Abdul_Alhazred); a living 2502 ruler is unverified, so use his disciples if needed.
flag_brief: A silver astrolabe encircling a skull-shaped crescent above a green open scroll on black violet
enclave_description: Abdul Alhazred studies forbidden lore in an observatory at Sharikah. Once educated alongside a Caliph's sons, the Mad Sorcerer became obsessed with Nehekhara, stole an artifact from his patron, and sought knowledge among its ruined cities. Here his disciples pursue necromancy and bargains with djinn, hiding books and experiments that the followers of Anmar Fakir would consign to the flames.

name: Moon-Well Keepers
placement: Zafira Oasis, east of Martek.
description: An old desert priesthood rejects the Prophet's revelation and fortifies surviving shrines against missionaries and tax collectors.
basis: **Made up;** old-faith opposition follows the mod's local premise.
flag_brief: A silver crescent cradling a small gold oasis palm above three white water rings on midnight blue
enclave_description: Nadir al-Qamar's Moon-Well Keepers guard the old shrines of Zafira Oasis. They preserve the rites of Nehekhara's gods and reject the Prophet's demand that those devotions yield to the One Faith. Pilgrims and fugitives find shelter behind their walls, while missionaries and tax collectors meet closed gates and armed worshippers prepared to defend the sacred wells.

name: Free Spears of the Copper Dunes
placement: Dhiban, east of El-Kalabad in Sudenburg's coastal territory; proposed former slave depot.
description: Escaped soldiers invoke the Prophet's universal message against hereditary slaveholders, creating an aggressive internal religious-political revolt.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: Three copper spearheads rising above a broken ivory shackle on sand-white, teal lower band
history_file: history/countries/E33 - Free Spears of the Copper Dunes.txt
enclave_description: Hamid al-Nahas leads escaped soldiers and slaves from a fortified refuge near Dhiban. His Free Spears invoke the One Faith's promise of a message for all peoples against the masters who once owned them. They raid slave caravans, arm those they release, and seize supplies from estates whose wealth rests on bondage, turning each rescue into another challenge to the surrounding rulers.

name: Court of the Cursed Scarab
placement: Khepesh, in the desert northeast of Numas and outside the royal capital.
description: Apophas becomes the focus of a death cult hunting souls rather than restoring a normal royal domain.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Apophas](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Prince_Apophas); a permanent court and followers are invented.
flag_brief: A gold winged scarab carrying an ivory skull disc on dark amethyst, turquoise border
history_file: history/countries/E34 - Court of the Cursed Scarab.txt
enclave_description: Apophas, the Cursed Scarab Lord, haunts the burial places of Khepesh in a shifting body of beetles. Condemned after murdering the royal family of Numas, he bargained with Usirian to find a soul that could replace his own. His hunt has no possible end, yet every caravan and settlement within reach offers another victim whom the desperate prince believes may free him.

name: Rikek Ash-Warrens
placement: Cripple Peak's cavern province, south of Nagashizzar itself.
description: Descendants of a nearly destroyed clan raid Nagashi tombs for warpstone and revenge, refusing absorption by stronger clans.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Clan Rikek](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/List_of_Skaven_clans); continued organized survival is speculative.
flag_brief: A lime-green angular rat skull above a shattered black pyramid on ash brown
enclave_description: Skreev Ashsnout leads the Rikek remnant through the ash-choked warrens beneath Cripple Peak. The survivors cling to their clan's name while scavenging the margins of Nagash's domain for warpstone and forgotten weapons. Tomb raids bring them into conflict with the undead, while stolen tribute and murdered envoys keep stronger Skaven clans from making obedient servants of them.

name: Black Oasis Riders
placement: Phaktra, immediately west of Numas; the enclave's oasis is a proposed local feature.
description: Living frontier riders destroy tomb patrols and raid burial stores, treating the awakened kings as unlawful possessors of their homeland.
basis: **Made up;** not the existing Scythanian realm.
flag_brief: A black palm tree over two crossed silver curved sabres on ochre, white sun above
enclave_description: Salim al-Rimal's Black Oasis Riders shelter among the living communities around Phaktra. They reject the authority of dead kings over the wells and grazing grounds on which their families depend. Mounted raiders break into burial stores and intercept tomb caravans, drawing provisions from the ancient wealth of Nehekhara while provoking the rulers who still claim it.

name: Clan Festerlingus
placement: Cuexotl Wilds, a concealed jungle warren outside Cuexotl's capital.
description: An additional named Skaven clan could supply a local plague power outside the already represented clan network.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Festerlingus in the Southlands](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/List_of_Skaven_clans); exact warren and Pestilens affinity proposed.
flag_brief: An ivory crocodile-rat skull with three green pustules on a muddy yellow field
enclave_description: Pustik Rotthroat's Clan Festerlingus has hollowed a plague refuge beneath the Cuexotl Wilds. Its Skaven carry Pestilens rites into the jungle, fouling water and raiding the approaches to Lizardmen sacred sites. The clan's small warrens cannot withstand the great powers around them in open war, so disease and ambush prepare the ground for every advance.

name: Hellbeard's Cinder Anchorage
placement: Scaleback Coast, on the eastern Southlands shore northeast of the Fortress of Dawn.
description: A surviving fleet detachment builds a slave-powered repair harbor and raids both the coast and Elven shipping.
basis: **Made up remnant;** inspired by [Abnagg Hellbeard's expedition](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Abnagg_Hellbeard).
flag_brief: A brass bull skull with a smoking black beard above crossed anchors on deep rust red
enclave_description: Abnagg Hellbeard's followers hold a smoke-stained anchorage on the Scaleback Coast. The surviving corsairs of his Chaos Dwarf venture repair their vessels with slave labor and trade stolen cargo for the supplies their distant homeland cannot provide. Their raiders hunt coastal traffic and Elven shipping, dragging captives back to workshops where the furnaces burn through the night.

name: Root-Eye Brood
placement: Nahuontl Peaks, a jungle-clad coastal escarpment on the western Southlands shore.
description: Spider-riding clans undermine larger Greenskin rulers and raid coastal traders from inaccessible canopy settlements.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A pale yellow spider with a green single eye, legs turning into roots on burnt umber
enclave_description: Zikrit Rootfang's Forest Goblins nest among the trees and broken slopes of the Nahuontl Peaks. Their Root-Eye Brood worships the spiders that carry its hunters through the canopy, above the roads watched by larger Greenskin tribes. Ambushed traders supply metal and captives, while poisoned arrows answer any Orc boss who demands that the brood surrender its independence.

name: River of Teeth Covenant
placement: Flooded Jungle, on the inland side of the Mangrove Coast; proposed river stronghold.
description: A vampire household poses as river guardians while demanding blood tribute and controlling transport through crocodile-haunted channels.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An ivory fanged jaw encircling a crimson river droplet on dark indigo, silver wave border
enclave_description: Zafira Nightwater's vampires hold hidden courts along the channels of the Flooded Jungle. The River of Teeth Covenant presents its members as guardians who keep worse dangers from the water, collecting blood in return for passage and protection. Boatmen who refuse the bargain disappear among the reeds, and the villages along the banks learn to provision a court they rarely see by daylight.

name: Braugh's Corpse-Train
placement: Brimstone Pass, on the Dark Lands approach to the Mountains of Mourn.
description: Braugh's enchanted chains keep slaves working after death, producing an Ogre enclave with a distinctive undead labor economy.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Braugh Slavelord](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Braugh_Slavelord); fixed base proposed.
flag_brief: An ivory ogre skull trailing three broken iron chains over a black wagon wheel on dark bronze
enclave_description: Braugh Slavelord keeps his shuffling captive train near Brimstone Pass. After escaping a necromancer's dungeon, the Ogre took enchanted chains whose victims remain bound to his service even after death. Living prisoners and corpses now haul his possessions together, while his raiders seize fresh captives from the mountain traffic to replace those too broken to move.

name: Sneaky Gits of Gash Kadrak
placement: Zharr Outskirts, east-southeast of Zharr-Naggrund; substitute foothold for Gash Kadrak, which has no separately named province.
description: A named slave-mining and assassination tribe can act as a treacherous client with ambitions against its patrons.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Sneaky Gits](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Sneaky_Git) and [Gash Kadrak](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Gash_Kadrak).
flag_brief: Two long white poisoned knives flanking a sly green goblin face on black, lime trim
history_file: history/countries/E42 - Sneaky Gits of Gash Kadrak.txt
enclave_description: Nagrit Shivtail's Sneaky Gits work from the Zharr Outskirts, drawing wealth and influence from the slave pits of Gash Kadrak. These Hobgoblins thrive as overseers, informers, and hired killers under Chaos Dwarf protection. Their knives enforce bargains that their patrons prefer to leave unrecorded, while hidden stores and private loyalties give the gang room to plot against anyone who trusts it.

name: Black Tally Rebellion
placement: Blackfire, a cavern and foundry satellite immediately beside the Tower of Gorgoth.
description: Escaped forge soldiers seize their former barracks and turn the industrial transport network against slave overseers.
basis: **Made up;** distinct from existing Broken Chainz and Ironclad Skulls.
flag_brief: A white broken slave collar over a black clenched orc fist on rust red, five slash marks below
enclave_description: Grakk Chainbreaker's Black Orcs occupy an armed refuge in Blackfire. Forged for obedience and war, these escaped soldiers have turned their discipline against the overseers who once counted them as property. They raid industrial roads for weapons and food, free useful captives, and keep the names of their former masters on the black tally that gives the rebellion its name.

name: Unchained Furnace
placement: Black Smoke Peaks, on the western Plain of Bones; proposed ruined mine.
description: Freed Dwarf captives renounce Hashut and launch rescue raids, creating an ideological enemy within Chaos Dwarf territory.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A silver anvil rising from a broken gold chain on deep teal, red furnace flame above
enclave_description: Dorin Shacklecleaver's freed Dwarfs have rekindled the ancestor shrines of a hidden hold in the Black Smoke Peaks. The Unchained Furnace rejects Hashut and the slave forges that supplied its founders with years of captivity. Its warriors ambush labor columns and carry rescued prisoners uphill, taking tools and weapons from the same workshops they now seek to undermine.

name: Ghuth's Spawnchompers
placement: Bloodpeak, in the northern, Chaos-exposed Mountains of Mourn.
description: Mutated Ogres deliberately eat Chaos creatures and accept Dragon Ogres, setting them apart from ordinary neighboring tribes.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Great Tribe of Ghuth Spawnchomper](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Great_Tribe_of_Ghuth_Spawnchomper).
flag_brief: A white ogre jaw biting a purple many-tentacled creature on black-orange
enclave_description: Ghuth Spawnchomper's Ogres feast on Chaos-tainted flesh around Bloodpeak. Their appetite for spawn has left its mark upon their bodies, and creatures shunned by other tribes gather around a camp where mutation is no obstacle to belonging. Dragon Ogres and malformed brutes add their strength to Ghuth's raiders, who descend on neighboring camps in search of the next extraordinary meal.

name: Bezer's Small Empire
placement: Gutbuster's Gate, a Gnoblar breakaway foothold within Goldtooth's territory.
description: A scheming Gnoblar power broker gains a playable petty realm; independence would turn service to Ogres into sabotage and rebellion.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Bezer's two-and-a-half-tribe empire](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Gnoblar); independent hostility and faith mapping proposed.
flag_brief: A tiny green goblin in an oversized golden crown standing on a white mushroom on burgundy
enclave_description: Bezer proclaims his small empire from the hiding places around Gutbuster's Gate. A Gnoblar ruler credited with uniting two and a half tribes, he offers his followers the rare prospect of serving someone who does not intend to eat them. Stolen food, concealed traps, and raids on Ogre stores keep his boast alive, irritating far larger neighbors who struggle to pin down their tiny adversaries.

name: White Hunger
placement: Choketooth Vale, a glacier above the central Mourn caravan passes.
description: Snow predators hold a mountain refuge and descend during storms to destroy caravans and lowland Ogre camps.
basis: **Made up pack;** [Yhetees' high-mountain habitat](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Yhetee) is canonical.
flag_brief: An ivory shaggy Yhetee head with ice-blue eyes and long claws on cold charcoal, glacier chevrons
enclave_description: Urrgh Whiteclaw's Yhetees haunt the frozen heights above Choketooth Vale. The White Hunger moves with the storms, descending on caravan camps when snow and darkness separate the guards from their fires. Ogre hunters enter the high passes to prove their strength, but abandoned weapons and frozen remains show how often the hunting runs the other way.

name: Last Hearth of the Tall Ones
placement: Giant's Ridge, in the western Mourn highlands; proposed surviving fragment of the ancient Giant Holds.
description: Giant survivors occupy defensible ruins and prey on Ogre settlers occupying their ancestral country.
basis: **Made up remnant polity.**
flag_brief: An enormous ivory hand sheltering a small orange hearth flame beneath a stone arch on earth brown
history_file: history/countries/E48 - Last Hearth of the Tall Ones.txt
enclave_description: Hrol Hearthkeeper's Giants cling to ancestral ruins along Giant's Ridge. Their gathering preserves the memory of a country overrun by Ogre expansion, feeding its resentment with each new camp raised among the broken stones. Raids on Ogre herds and settlements supply the Last Hearth, while tales told around its fires give dispossessed wanderers a reason to remain and fight.

name: Oglah Khan's Exiles
placement: Heicheng, a highland camp northwest of the Great Bastion's western approaches.
description: A banished mercenary band opposes the ruling khan and sells its service across the frontier.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Oglah Khan](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Oglah_Khan); this deliberately relocates his Old World mercenary activity.
flag_brief: A snarling black wolf head inside a golden horseshoe on pale yellow, red arrow below
enclave_description: Oglah Khan's wolf-riders camp near Heicheng, selling the speed and ferocity that once served the Hobgobla Khan. Oglah lost that patronage when he changed sides at Xen-Tu and found he had backed the defeated army. Exile made him a mercenary; now neighboring rulers bid for his services, while his riders provision themselves from a frontier that cannot easily keep them out.

name: Ash-Hoof Herd
placement: Tuoba, just beyond the Great Bastion; use a local scrub refuge within the steppe province.
description: Mounted Beastmen prey on horse-breeding camps and try to displace the human and Hobgoblin riders around them.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A red cloven hoof stamping an ivory skull on black, brass flames below
enclave_description: Khorgh Ashhoof's Centigors range across the pasturelands of Tuoba, carrying skulls and torn harnesses back to their gathering grounds. The Ash-Hoof Herd worships Khorne through close slaughter, falling upon horse camps and isolated riders before larger forces can assemble. Human and Hobgoblin herders alike lose animals and kin, while the herd claims each bloodied stretch of grass as another victory over settled rule.

name: Broken Harness Freehold
placement: Icescar, where the western steppe meets the northern Mourn approaches.
description: Escaped captives and deserters defend an unusual mixed settlement, raiding slave caravans while rejecting both khan and imperial governor.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A broken bronze horse harness encircling two crossed silver farm spears on muted jade
enclave_description: Shun Liu's Broken Harness Freehold shelters escaped captives and deserters behind the stockades of Icescar. Its inhabitants come from both sides of the frontier and bind themselves through mutual defense rather than service to a khan or governor. They attack slave caravans and hide those they free, making their settlement a refuge to the hunted and a provocation to every authority that claims them.

name: Cult of the Painted Skin
placement: Xienxen, a rural foothold in the Sea Court's territory; substitute for the unmapped Bei-Chai district.
description: A documented clandestine cult gains a rural power base, infiltrating officials and attacking the Dragon court's enforcement network.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Beichai](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Beichai); Tzeentch is a gameplay choice amid the cult's ambiguous patronage.
flag_brief: A white theatrical face mask split to reveal a turquoise staring eye on deep purple, red paint brush below
history_file: history/countries/E52 - Cult of the Painted Skin.txt
enclave_description: Xiu Shen's Painted Skin cult has woven itself into the households and offices of Xienxen. Its traditions reach back to the secret Chaos worship associated with Beichai, where outward respectability concealed devotion to forbidden powers. Here the cult serves the Changer of Ways through bribery, stolen identities, and concealed rites, using official seals and polite invitations to reach places an armed invader could not.

name: Vermilion Tax Revolt
placement: Radiant Plains, a farmland district in the Celestial Riverlands.
description: Armed farmers claim corrupt officials have broken harmony, confiscating grain and fighting collection armies while respecting the cosmological order.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A white broken tally stick crossed with a rice sickle on vermilion red, gold rice stalks
enclave_description: Bao Zhang's followers hold grain stores and fortified villages in the Radiant Plains. The Vermilion Tax Revolt began among farmers who saw corrupt collectors empty their granaries while speaking solemnly of Harmony. Its militias now seize revenue convoys and destroy tax registers, claiming that defense of the proper order requires resistance to the officials appointed to uphold it.

name: Jade Coffin Society
placement: Minghua, southwest of Wei-Jin; proposed ancestral-tomb enclave outside the capital.
description: A criminal vampire society rejects the Jiangshi Court's negotiated status and openly takes control of burial villages.
basis: **Made up;** intentionally separate from the existing Jiangshi state.
flag_brief: A jade-green upright coffin sealed with gold talismans between two white bat wings on black
enclave_description: Mei Jiang's Jade Coffin Society rules a concealed world of graveyards, smugglers, and indebted households in Minghua. Its vampires disregard the restraints and ceremonies by which the Jiangshi Court maintains its place among Cathay's rulers. Kidnapping and illicit burial work supply their hunger, while paid accomplices keep the dead moving through streets where respectable officials insist nothing is amiss.

name: Copper Tail Refuge
placement: Sapphire Grove, in southern Cathay north of the Monkey Court's core.
description: A splinter clan refuses both Monkey King and Dragon officials, raiding pilgrimage roads to fund an independent sanctuary.
basis: **Made up;** not a duplicate of the Monkey Court.
flag_brief: A copper monkey tail coiling around a white refuge gate on forest green
enclave_description: Kavi Copper-Tail leads an independent Monkeyfolk refuge in Sapphire Grove. His followers reject both the Dragon rulers' demands for obedience and the Monkey King's claim to speak for all their kind. From concealed paths above the pilgrim roads they seize provisions and tribute, using the grove's heights to frustrate soldiers sent by patrons they have already refused.

name: Bengals of the Tiger's Eye
placement: Kushan, in northern Ind's hills; proposed cave foothold because the Eye of the Tiger is not separately mapped.
description: A hostile tiger-headed tribe occupies a legendary cave, demanding offerings and attacking treasure hunters and royal expeditions.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Ind's Bengal tribe](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Ind); keeps the mod's Tigerkin distinct from uniformly Chaotic Beastmen.
flag_brief: A golden tiger face with a single emerald eye and black stripes on warm ivory, dark green border
history_file: history/countries/E56 - Bengals of the Tiger's Eye.txt
enclave_description: Rajar Stripeclaw's Bengals guard the caves and forest paths of Kushan. The Tiger's Eye tribe belongs to Ind's older jungle world, where sacred beasts and their descendants command offerings from neighboring communities. Treasure seekers and hunters who intrude upon its caverns meet claws and spears, while disputes over tribute and access to the forest keep the tribe at odds with the surrounding courts.

name: Red Banquet Court
placement: Panchala, on the western side of the Bone Eaters' northern Ind territory.
description: Vampiric Ogres demand blood and provisions from surrounding villages, opposing both neighboring rajahs and ordinary Ogre tribes.
basis: **Made up dynasty;** the mod's [Lore Reference](./Examples/Lore%20Reference.txt) explicitly supports vampiric Ogres in northern Ind.
flag_brief: An ivory ogre skull with fangs above a gold chalice overflowing with red on deep purple
enclave_description: Gorakka Redgullet's vampiric Ogres keep a lavish court in Panchala. Their banquets consume cattle and blood alike, with tribute brought from villages too exposed to refuse the invitation. Rajahs resent the loss of revenue and subjects, while living Ogre rivals find their strength challenged by cousins whose hunger continues beyond death and whose household grows with every successful hunt.

name: Ash Lotus Ascetics
placement: Kushari Plains, in northern Ind; the cremation island is a proposed local feature, not a separately mapped island.
description: A death-seeking sect has crossed into necromancy, raising discarded bodies and rejecting the authority of temple and prince alike.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A silver lotus holding a small black skull and rising gray smoke on dark violet
enclave_description: Harendra Ashlotus gathers outcast ascetics around the cremation grounds of the Kushari Plains. Their pursuit of release from mortal limits has led them into necromancy, turning funeral rites into experiments upon the remains entrusted to them. Temple authorities condemn the sect, but its disciples steal ashes, bodies, and sacred vessels while a growing company of the dead guards their retreat.

name: Emerald Throat Brood
placement: Ceylon, a jungle foothold inside Singha's territory beside the Khureshi frontier.
description: A displaced serpent household establishes a captive-hunting frontier enclave inside human territory.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A gold cobra with an emerald throat gem and forked ivory tongue on black-green
enclave_description: Ssaritha Emerald-Throat's displaced Snakefolk household has taken refuge in the tangled forests of Ceylon. Denied the security of a greater serpent court, it survives through hidden shrines, captive labor, and raids on the human communities along its margins. Prisoners are carried inland for service and sacrifice, while the brood's venomous hunters punish anyone who follows their trail.

name: Moltless Sepulchre
placement: Dragonfall, beside the Blood Queen's ruined-city capital; proposed sealed temple enclave.
description: Renegade priests replace living transformation with preserved undeath, stealing eggs and royal corpses from neighboring broods.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An ivory snake skeleton coiled around a black funeral urn on dark jade
enclave_description: Ssilak Moltless rules a forbidden sepulchre in Dragonfall, where Snakefolk adepts preserve dead flesh instead of surrendering it to decay and renewal. They steal eggs, ancestral remains, and the corpses of royal servants for rites condemned by rival serpent courts. Their hidden chambers hold the promise of an unchanging existence, paid for with raids upon the living lineages around them.

name: Unbitten League
placement: Silvermist Hills, in the jungles of western Khuresh.
description: Escaped human prey build a defended refuge and raid captive columns, making a rare human resistance state in Snakefolk country.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: Two silver hands breaking a golden serpent-shaped shackle on crimson, blue lower band
enclave_description: Devendra Nagesh's Unbitten League holds palisaded refuges in the Silvermist Hills. Its founders escaped the captive pens of Khuresh and learned to hide villages where serpent patrols struggle to follow. They ambush prisoner columns and guide survivors uphill, striking at the traffic that sustains nearby courts while refusing to accept that humans must remain prey.

name: Hollow Gong Warren
placement: Silent Lotus, a proposed temple-road burrow in Longfangs territory.
description: A secluded rat clan sabotages ritual traffic and steals the venom stores on which neighboring Snakefolk courts depend.
basis: **Made up;** not the existing Clan Eskemas.
flag_brief: A black rat triangle cut through a bronze gong with a green crack on charcoal
enclave_description: Chikkit Gonggnaw's Skaven burrow beneath the shrines and waterways of Silent Lotus. The Hollow Gong Warren steals venom from Snakefolk stores and undermines the causeways used by ritual processions. Poisoned blades and sudden collapses conceal a small clan's weakness, allowing Gonggnaw to plunder temple traffic while stronger enemies search the jungle above his tunnels.

name: Mangrove Eye Court
placement: Zhanggan Wetlands, on southern Khuresh's western coast.
description: A displaced Fimir household competes with serpent courts for captives, using sea fog to conceal night raids.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A single gold eye above a white hooked blade and mangrove roots on black teal
enclave_description: Morrga Mangrove-Eye's Fimir hold a mist-shrouded court in the Zhanggan Wetlands. Their raiders cross drowned channels at night, taking captives from villages and rival serpent households before withdrawing beyond the firm ground. The court's power rests on waters few outsiders can navigate, and every abandoned boat adds to the warning against entering its fog.

name: Empty Sheath League
placement: Spirit of the Crane, a mountain province in central Nippon.
description: Warrior monks shelter peasants and refuse all daimyo levies, spreading revolt from a defensible religious stronghold.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An empty black sword scabbard between two white reed stalks on pale gray-blue, small crimson sun
enclave_description: Akihiro Kuroda's Empty Sheath League shelters peasants and masterless fighters around the fortified temples of Spirit of the Crane. Its warrior monks refuse the levies of competing daimyo, arguing that no lord has earned obedience by bringing another war to the fields. Armed processions guard the roads, and grain owed to neighboring castles feeds refugees behind the temple gates.

name: Cinder-Eye Burrow
placement: Iseki, a mountain foothold in southern Nippon; proposed volcanic workings outside Takai's capital.
description: Small Greenskins monopolize sulfur workings and use explosive ambushes against samurai patrols and rival goblins.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A gold slit eye inside an orange flame over crossed white tunnel picks on charcoal
enclave_description: Skarrik Cinder-Eye's Kobolds occupy sulfur workings beneath Iseki. The burrow turns stolen tools and dangerous powders into traps for the samurai patrols and Goblin rivals that seek to drive it out. Smoke seeps from cracks above the workshops, while attacks on pack trains keep the little forges supplied and the mountain roads under constant threat.

name: Antlered Hunger
placement: Ixtoc, in the interior highlands of northern Elithis; proposed forest refuge.
description: A Beastman enclave raids Elven settlements and wrecked ships, challenging colonial control beyond the defended coast.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An ivory antlered goat skull above a jagged red mouth on black-brown
enclave_description: Ghorak Thornhorn's Caprigor herd lurks in the forests of Ixtoc, scavenging the wrecks and abandoned camps along the coast. The Antlered Hunger treats the Elven colonies as a spreading trespass, tearing down boundary markers and hunting parties sent beyond the settled clearings. Captured tools arm the herd, and each failed expedition leaves more spoils beneath its crude shrines.

name: Unmoored Spears
placement: Elithis Outpost, on the southern island coast.
description: Soldiers abandoned by their patrons turn to predatory warrior cults and raid the colonies they once defended.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: Three silver elven spearheads rising from a severed gold anchor chain on deep blue
enclave_description: Aelar Wavebreaker's Unmoored Spears hold a renegade camp in Elithis Outpost. Once charged with defending Asur settlements, these abandoned soldiers have turned toward the darker gods of the Cytharai and the profits of armed predation. Their knowledge of watch posts, warehouses, and coastal tracks lets them raid the same communities whose safety was once their duty.

name: Itz-Itza
placement: Pyooshupya, an unowned outlying Dragon Isle.
description: Adapt the named tribe as stubborn old-faith survivors, creating a religious contrast with neighboring dragon-tribute courts.
basis: Total War adaptation — [Itz-Itza Tribe](https://warhammerfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Itz-Itza_Tribe); the old-faith opposition is invented.
flag_brief: An ivory stepped pyramid beneath a jade reptile eye and small gold sun on turquoise-black
enclave_description: Itz-Huax's followers preserve the worship of the Old Ones in Pyooshupya. Surrounded by Dragon Isles clans that offer blood and treasure to living dragons, the Itz-Itza guard old tablets and spawning rites as remnants of an order their neighbors have forsaken. Rival priests covet their sacred places, while Itz-Huax's warriors resist tribute demands and strike at those who would turn the shrines into dragon altars.

name: River-Ruin Chainport
placement: Noigo, on the northern shore of Honzamul facing the River Ruin approaches.
description: A slave-raiding naval foothold threatens the clans through iron ships, fortified docks, and captive labor.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A brass chain forming an anchor below a red smoking bull head on soot gray
enclave_description: Zarkhul Ironwake's Chaos Dwarfs have fortified the docks of Noigo at the mouth of the River Ruin. Their chainport shelters iron vessels, slave pens, and workshops that turn island timber and stolen labor into provisions for further voyages. Raiding parties seize captives from neighboring scale-clans, making the harbor a permanent foothold for the slavers of the river.

name: Cave of the First Hunger
placement: Xcha, in the interior of Honzamul; proposed cave system beneath the island.
description: Cave dwellers emerge against both clan settlements and foreign mines, adding an underground monster society to the islands.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An ivory primitive reptile jaw emerging from a black cave mouth on ochre with red handprints
history_file: history/countries/E70 - Cave of the First Hunger.txt
enclave_description: Gor-Ulk's Troglodytes inhabit the deep caves beneath Xcha. Their hunting bands emerge along forgotten passages to raid island clans, gem workings, and foreign mining camps. Food and captives disappear into chambers beyond the reach of daylight, while repeated attacks prevent any surface ruler from treating the ground above the caves as secure territory.

name: Scourge of Khaine
placement: Darkspire, a northern Nagarythe coastal foothold outside Tor Anlec.
description: A Druchii religious-military foothold attacks the surrounding Asur kingdoms and threatens routes through the mountain gates.
basis: Total War adaptation — [Scourge of Khaine](https://totalwarwarhammer.fandom.com/wiki/Scourge_of_Khaine).
flag_brief: A silver serrated elven sword with a red handprint over black, crimson corner triangles
enclave_description: Nocrusith's Scourge of Khaine maintains a Druchii foothold in Darkspire. Its warriors carry the Murder God's worship into Ulthuan, using fortified heights and guarded tracks to threaten the roads through the surrounding mountains. Raids bring captives and supplies back to the stronghold, while its continued survival mocks the Asur lords who claim to have secured their homeland.

name: Cult of Excess
placement: Circle of Night, a secluded estate district in southern Ulthuan.
description: A forbidden pleasure cult operates inside Asur society, using aristocratic wealth to sustain armed resistance and abductions.
basis: Total War adaptation — [Cult of Excess](https://totalwarwarhammer.fandom.com/wiki/Cult_of_Excess), distinct from Morathi's existing realm.
flag_brief: A golden chalice with a pink serpent winding around its stem on deep purple, silver crescent above
enclave_description: Arathar's Cult of Excess hides armed devotees among the secluded estates of the Circle of Night. Wealth and cultivated taste conceal a Slaaneshi circle whose private indulgences demand servants, victims, and ever greater freedom from restraint. Abductions feed its rites, while influential patrons keep inquiries from reaching the doors behind which their neighbors disappear.

name: Blackfang's Worshippers
placement: Arithor, in the Ellyrian hills at the Annulii's western approaches; a foothill cave substitute for the impassable high peaks.
description: A Beastman cult venerates the memory of an infamous local Chimera and captures travelers as offerings.
basis: **Made up cult;** [Blackfang of the Annulii](https://warhammerfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Chimera) is the inspiration, not assumed alive.
flag_brief: An ivory fanged beast skull crowned with black antlers on dark violet, blood-red lower slash
enclave_description: Gharr Blackfang's Beastmen have made the wild approaches of Arithor a shrine to the terror of Blackfang, the Chimera of the Annulii. The beast's legend gives their scattered raiders a common idol and a reason to gather trophies from the mountain roads. Travelers are carried to crude altars, and each unanswered raid strengthens the herd's claim that the heights belong to monsters.

name: Blackpine Autarii
placement: Skarnshade, east of Clar Karond in the Black Forest region.
description: Independent Shade families attack tax expeditions and intercept slaves, refusing incorporation into the city nobility's estates.
basis: **Made up clan;** inspired by [Shades' independent origins](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Shade).
flag_brief: A silver pine tree crossed with two black daggers on pale cold green, crimson eye in trunk
enclave_description: Draleth Blackpine leads Shade families in the trackless country around Skarnshade. These Autarii preserve the independence of Naggaroth's wilderness clans, rejecting the taxes and commands of distant city lords. They intercept slave columns and supply trains, sell what they seize, and vanish into terrain that punishes the heavily armed expeditions sent to bring them to heel.

name: Hotek's Lost Apprentices
placement: Shadowfrost, a pass through the Iron Mountains; uses a traversable foothold instead of the impassable Iron Mountains province.
description: Renegade smiths preserve forbidden rune experiments and raid royal workshops, turning craft secrecy into a rival mountain power.
basis: **Made up order;** inspired by [Hotek](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Hotek), not a claim Hotek himself rebelled.
flag_brief: A silver hammer striking a gold star atop a dark anvil on midnight blue, pale runic border without letters
enclave_description: Vaelir Ashforge's renegade smiths work in concealed foundries in Shadowfrost. Claiming the legacy of Hotek, they seek mastery of forbidden runes and weapons beyond the supervision of Naggaroth's rulers. Raids on royal workshops provide metal, tools, and skilled captives, while secret commissions give ambitious patrons reason to protect artisans they would publicly condemn.

name: Deadwood Unbound
placement: Deadwood, a forest province on Naggaroth's northeastern frontier.
description: Escaped foreign captives fortify the timber works and attack both Druchii recapture parties and northern raiders.
basis: **Made up;** not the conventional Druchii Deadwood Sentinels faction.
flag_brief: A silver wood axe breaking a black chain around a white pine tree on dark red-brown
enclave_description: Hakon Freedhand's fugitives have fortified the timber works of Deadwood. Escaped foreign captives use the tools of their former labor to raise palisades, stock provisions, and prepare for the slavers' return. Rescue raids bring new hands into the settlement, while Druchii masters and opportunistic Norse raiders watch for a chance to seize the people sheltering behind its walls.

name: Rimejaw Families
placement: Nightair, a northern mountain pass above Naggaroth's military approaches.
description: Cold-adapted trolls feast on baggage trains and refuse the beastmasters who attempt to cage them.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A white troll jaw with icicle tusks over three black pine trees on glacial blue
enclave_description: Rulgh Rimejaw's Troll families shelter in the frozen gullies of Nightair. Driven to resist the beastmasters who would chain them, they feed on baggage trains, herd animals, and patrols separated from their support. Their scattered dens make a single decisive hunt difficult, while every unattended carcass draws more of the clan down from the cold heights.

name: Vashnaar's Foothold
placement: Gorepeak, inland from S'sildra Tor on the southern Naggaroth approaches to Lustria.
description: A mixed Chaos–Druchii force builds a staging enclave for raids and a later attack on the Lizardmen.
basis: Lore/Total War adaptation — [Vashnaar's Conquest](https://totalwarwarhammer.fandom.com/wiki/Vashnaar%27s_Conquest). His recorded Lustrian invasion is 2521; this 2502 base is speculative.
flag_brief: A silver horned elven helm pierced by a red eight-pointed star on black violet
enclave_description: Vashnaar the Tormentor has established a gathering ground at Gorepeak for Chaos warriors and Druchii adventurers. His followers combine the strength of armored northern fighters with the cruelty and discipline of Naggaroth's exiles. Raids provision the camp and recruit captives for its labor gangs, while Vashnaar turns his attention toward the wealth and ancient cities of Lustria.

name: Cylostra's Drowned
placement: Blightward, a haunted southern Naggaroth coastal foothold north of the Isthmus.
description: A ghostly court and drowned crew prey on shipping, offering a supernatural rival to ordinary Druchii slavers.
basis: Total War adaptation — [The Drowned](https://totalwarwarhammer.fandom.com/wiki/The_Drowned); exact shore base and religion mapping proposed.
flag_brief: A silver ghostly opera mask wearing a shell crown above turquoise waves on deep midnight blue
enclave_description: Cylostra Direfin's drowned court haunts the shore of Blightward. The Bretonnian singer's death at sea left her bound to an audience and crew who can no longer escape the performance. Ghostly sailors and waterlogged dead raid the coast in her service, threatening shipping and competing with Druchii slavers for the living who still dare to approach her waters.

name: Azure Fang Brood
placement: Tlacox, an Isthmus hill province within S'sildra Tor's frontier territory.
description: A cut-off spawning community defends ancient sites and attacks Druchii settlement, distinct from the Slann-ruled states farther south.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: A white reptile fang ring surrounding a golden sun-eye on vivid azure blue with black stepped trim
enclave_description: Tzak-Huax leads the Azure Fang Brood around the ancient sites of Tlacox. Isolated from the guidance of the great temple-cities, its Lizardmen defend spawning grounds and ruined sanctuaries through inherited custom and immediate necessity. Druchii logging parties and settlers meet ambushes beyond their clearings, while the brood dismantles new works raised on ground it has guarded for generations.

name: Port Reaver
placement: The named Port Reaver province on Lustria's northeastern coast.
description: A pirate port under an elected or appointed sea captain, attacking shipping and sponsoring expeditions into Lizardmen territory.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Port Reaver](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Port_Reaver); the culture and religion are gameplay choices for its mixed population.
flag_brief: A white skull above crossed silver cutlasses on black, small gold palm frond behind the skull
enclave_description: Lorenzo Saltavento's sea captains hold the quays and storehouses of Port Reaver. The settlement traces its founding to Lucciano Soprania, who established the pirate haven in 1801 after losing his position on Sartosa. Its present crews live by stolen cargo and expeditions into Lustria, turning a precarious coastal foothold into a market for plunder that neighboring powers cannot easily control.

name: Swamp Town
placement: The named Swamp Town province on Lustria's northeastern coast.
description: A free trading town founded by fugitives and gamblers, defending its autonomy from pirates and temple-city armies. A less aggressive alternative.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Swamp Town](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Swamp_Town); preserve its comparatively safe trading character.
flag_brief: A gold stilt-house above three silver river waves with two white reeds on dark moss green
enclave_description: Konrad Reedhaven speaks for the traders, fugitives, and fortune seekers of Swamp Town. Its timber houses and muddy wharves offer a comparatively safe place to barter on a coast troubled by pirates and the dangers of Lustria. The townsfolk defend that freedom with armed watches and guarded stores, resisting outside rulers whose taxes or garrisons might turn a refuge into another possession.

name: Sven's River Company
placement: Xotlzax, on the navigable Amaxon waters beside Amazonia; a river-base substitute because Iquitos and the Amoco are not separately named on the mod map.
description: An expatriate engineer's river base gives Dwarfs a small industrial foothold, with armed river traffic provoking local Lizardmen.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Sven Hasselfriesian](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Sven_Hasselfriesian). A lasting company-state is proposed; the river settlement comes from older setting material.
flag_brief: A bronze dwarf face with a forked silver beard above a red paddlewheel on deep blue
enclave_description: Sven Hasselfriesian's river company maintains a fortified camp in Xotlzax. The exiled Dwarf engineer brought his appetite for invention to Lustria, where steamboats and stubborn crews carry explorers far beyond the coastal settlements. Their demands for fuel, salvage, and access to ancient sites draw resistance from the Lizardmen, but Sven's followers regard each obstacle as something to engineer or shoot their way through.

name: Bregonne
placement: Axmin, on the Amaxon delta west of Tlaxtlan; represents the otherwise unmapped Bretonnian hamlet.
description: A Bretonnian fort and settler community refuses the surrounding temple-city's authority and supports inland treasure hunting.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Bregonne](https://whfb-de.lexicanum.com/wiki/Bregonne), citing the Klaqulxol scenario; continued survival at the mod start is a design choice.
flag_brief: A white pegasus above a gold jungle leaf on quartered deep green and red
enclave_description: Marcel de Parravon's Bretonnian settlers hold a fortified foothold in Axmin under the name of Bregonne. Knights and adventurers have carried their familiar ranks and claims into a land whose temples they regard as sources of treasure. Stolen relics finance the settlement, while Lizardmen patrols contest every expedition sent beyond its walls to enlarge this distant piece of Bretonnia.

name: Nuevo Luccini
placement: Tzul'cata, on the northern Settler Coast southeast of Port Reaver and Swamp Town.
description: A Tilean pirate and robber settlement competes with other colonial ports and raids nearby river routes.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Lustria's settlements](https://warhammerfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Lustria); precise map placement proposed.
flag_brief: A gold leopard face above a white merchant ship on blue-green, red and ivory quarter corners
enclave_description: Marco Venturi's captains maintain Nuevo Luccini among the waterways of Tzul'cata. The Tilean settlement lives on river trade, piracy, and the sale of goods whose owners rarely accompany them to market. Competing colonial agents find willing smugglers behind its wharves, while armed crews resist attempts by neighboring authorities to inspect cargo or claim a share of the proceeds.

name: Amber Maw Expedition
placement: Xolt, on the jungle-covered western approaches to the southern Spine of Sotek.
description: Ogre mercenaries abandon their employers and establish hunting camps, consuming sacred beasts and raiding nearby spawning grounds.
basis: **Made up.**
flag_brief: An ivory ogre jaw biting an amber gemstone above crossed spears on dark jungle green
enclave_description: Borgut Ambermaw's Ogres have abandoned their employers and made their own camp in Xolt. The expedition feeds on the great beasts of Lustria and plunders the stores of anyone who ventures within reach. Sacred animals and guarded spawning pools hold no special claim on the Maneaters' restraint, bringing the camp into repeated conflict with the Lizardmen who defend them.

name: Ashen Plaque Covenant
placement: Xaltlan, northwest of Oxyl; proposed ruined observatory outside the temple-city capital.
description: Skink priests claim the Great Plan has failed and offer blood to living dragons, defying neighboring Slann.
basis: **Made up;** a dragon-worshipping schism among Lustrian Lizardmen.
flag_brief: A golden dragon curling around a black stepped stone plaque with an ember-red sun on charcoal
enclave_description: Xol-Tzek's Ashen Plaque Covenant holds dissident shrines in Xaltlan. Its Skink priests teach that the Slann's reading of the Great Plan has failed, and that living dragons must receive the blood once offered under older rites. Converts carry sacred objects into the renegade sanctuaries, while attacks on loyal temple servants turn a dispute over prophecy into open hostility.

name: Culchan Feather Exiles
placement: Southern Plains, on the northern edge of the Culchan Plains; proposed river-grove refuge.
description: An exiled Amazon warband rejects its queen's alliances and raids both temple estates and foreign settlements to fund an eventual return.
basis: **Made up;** a separate political faction, not a replacement for Amazonia.
flag_brief: Three broad magenta and turquoise bird feathers behind a golden spearhead on dark green
enclave_description: Itzara Culchanfeather's Amazon exiles range across the Southern Plains. Rejection of their queen's alliances has left them dependent on their own hunters, guarded camps, and swift raids. Temple stores and foreign expeditions provide supplies for the company, while captured weapons and growing bands of disaffected warriors sustain the hope of returning home on their own terms.

name: Deep Drum Hold
placement: Izaltl, a highland province in southern Lustria; proposed buried mine.
description: Descendants of a failed mining expedition claim the surrounding ore seams and attack temple-city labor parties as trespassers.
basis: **Made up;** no claim of a canonical Lustrian Dwarf kingdom.
flag_brief: A bronze war drum between two ivory hammers on deep purple, concentric cave arch border
enclave_description: Grundi Deepdrum's Dwarfs hold a secluded mine beneath Izaltl. Descendants of a lost expedition, they have made the workings a home and the surrounding ore deposits a claim recorded in their own books of possession. Lizardmen labor parties and temple guards dispute those rights, while Deepdrum's miners answer interference with fortified galleries and armed sorties into the jungle.

name: Clan Skaar
placement: Falco, immediately northeast of Pavona; a surface foothold representing a branch of Under-Pavona rather than taking Pavona's capital.
description: Warpstone suppliers play Moulder and Skryre against one another; their mine-state threatens both surface owners and rival buyers.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Clan Skaar](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Clan_Skaar).
flag_brief: A black rat triangle enclosing a bright green crystal above crossed bone mining picks on rust brown
enclave_description: Krizzik Oreclaw directs Clan Skaar's miners beneath Falco. The clan's wealth rests on warpstone, and its leaders play the needs of Moulder and Skryre against one another to avoid becoming the servants of either. Secret shafts reach toward fresh deposits while slave gangs haul the ore away, leaving subsidence, missing workers, and violent disputes beneath the surface settlements.

name: Clan Skaul
placement: Weissbuck, in Altdorf's western outskirts; represents an outlying burrow instead of the capital's central undercity.
description: A decadent clan turns warpstone addiction into leverage over neighbors, financing kidnappings and underground gang wars.
basis: Lore adaptation — [Clan Skaul](https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Clan_Skaul).
flag_brief: A white horned rat skull above a purple smoke bowl on black, ragged lime edge
enclave_description: Skaalrik Dreamfang's Clan Skaul burrows beneath Weissbuck.
